name: Napkin boxes
summary: Dots and boxes on a drawn café napkin for two: on your turn draw one line between two dots in your pen color, close a box and your face goes in it and you go again; when the napkin is full the one with more boxes wins the stake, and a new napkin starts with the loser.
useWhen: bored in line at kettle, play something
loser buys the chai, you're on
quick game while we wait for the bus
settle it with a game, winner picks dinner
dontUseWhen: a group game for more than two (use trivia-night or imposter)
a bet on something real happening (use handshake-bet)

place.description: Where the napkin is, e.g. 'Kettle & Crumb'; may be empty

players.description: The two players (names in the chat), first to move first

stake.description: What's on the line, e.g. 'Loser buys the chai'; may be empty

talk.description: One line of trash talk each, same order as players, in their words

moves.description: Lines already drawn, in order, as 'h' or 'v' then row then column digits, e.g. 'h00' (top edge of the first box) or 'v12'; played with the real turn rules
